subject.title: fix(infra): cap session-maintenance-warning dedupe cache with LRU eviction

question: Should session maintenance warning dedupe accept a private 4096-entry LRU cap, knowing evicted sessions may warn again after the cap is exceeded?
rationale: The code path is narrow and source-proven, but the patch intentionally changes message-delivery warning semantics for high-cardinality gateways.

options.title: Accept the private LRU cap
options.body: Merge after exact-head validation, preserving current behavior below 4096 entries while bounding long-running gateway memory growth.

options.title: Ask for a different lifecycle owner
options.body: Require a session-store-owned reset or different cap policy if warning delivery should not own eviction locally.

options.title: Pause for measured policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want production memory evidence or a broader cache policy before accepting this trade-off.

recommendation.title: Accept the private LRU cap
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head validation, preserving current behavior below 4096 entries while bounding long-running gateway memory growth.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the session maintenance warning delivery behavior and are the clearest feature-history owner for this warning-dedupe policy choice.
